clauses.reason: The sole paragraph adds subsection (d) to section 602 of Executive Order 10480: (d)(1) assigns to the Director of the Office of Management and Budget the President’s functions under section 309 of the Defense Production Act to prepare and submit offsets reports to Congress, and (d)(2) authorizes the United States International Trade Commission as central collection agency to collect the information for the first such report. Executive Order 12649 (signed 1988-08-11) deletes the text of section 602(d)(2) and inserts text naming the Bureau of Economic Analysis of the United States Department of Commerce for reports required by section 309; this is a strike-and-insert later event that changes the substance of (d)(2) and the clause continues, amended. Executive Order 12919 of June 3, 1994 provides in section 904: "(a) The following are superseded or revoked:" and lists "(9) Executive Order No. 12521 of June 24, 1985 (50 FR 26335).". That names this order and revokes or supersedes it. EO 12919 contains no effective-date wording for section 904, so the first-end date is its signing date, 1994-06-03; this is a reading of the text and not express wording.

EO 12649 (1988-08-11) strikes and replaces section 602(d)(2), the part of this order that names the International Trade Commission. Under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on strike-and-insert amendments, EO 12649 is a later event and the clause continues, amended.

savings.reason: The offsets reporting function was delegated again, to the Secretary of Commerce, by section 401 of EO 12919, so the function continues under an independent command of the later order; reports prepared under this order are accrued. No surviving command of EO 12521 itself is held.
